organization.name: BGZ care organization and practitioner
organization.purpose: Authorizing a BGZ retrieval on behalf of a practitioner

input_descriptors.name: Care organization identity from fake UZI-server certificate

fields.purpose: The credential must descend from this sandbox's own demo CA. A did:x509 proof establishes only that the chain inside the credential is self-consistent: the resolver takes chain[0] as the certificate to validate and builds its trust store out of chain[1:], both from the credential's own x5c header (nuts-node vdr/didx509/resolver.go), and its comment there says presentation definitions are where accepted CAs get limited. Without this field a requester generates its own CA, issues itself a leaf with any organization name and any URA, and satisfies every other field below. The CA is identified by fingerprint and by nothing else: subject: and san: assertions in a did:x509 policy string are evaluated against the leaf, which is entirely the requester's to choose. No id on this field, so it emits no claim, and no capture group, so nothing here resolves to a value; see sandbox/policy_test.go, TestBGZPolicyIssuerFieldIsUnnamedAndGroupFree, for why organization_id below is the opposite call under the same rule. The fingerprint is substituted by sandbox/generate-demo-certs.sh; a placeholder cannot be 43 base64url characters, so this file as committed denies everything.

Exactly one capture group, spanning the whole DID. The node resolves a field to its capture group when the pattern has one and to the whole match otherwise (nuts-node vcr/pe/presentation_definition.go, matchField's pattern branch), and this field has an id, so whatever it resolves to is emitted as the organization_id introspection claim. The earlier pattern ^did:web: had no group and matched only the prefix, so every organization was handed the constant "did:web:". Compare the $.issuer field above, which is group-free on purpose: same rule, opposite conclusion, because that field has no id and no value to emit.

input_descriptors.name: Sandbox practitioner context
input_descriptors.purpose: Establishing who is acting: the practitioner the requester signed in through Dezi, stated by the requesting organization itself. Self-asserted, so it is worth what the requester is worth: nothing checks it against Dezi or against the organization the token names. The PDP needs both values for the Mitz consent check (component/pdp/mitz.go).

input_descriptors.name: Sandbox organization context
input_descriptors.purpose: Carrying the facility type, which no other credential on this path supplies.
